blocks.heading: You're bidding on the same houses as everyone else.

columns.body:
Every flipper is competing for the same inventory and selling to the same retail buyer pool. Margins thin out, days on market stretch, and the exit depends on what a family with a mortgage will pay that month.

Co-living changes what a house is worth, because it changes who buys it. A property converted to shared housing sells to an investor pricing off room-level income, not comps down the street.

The catch is that the learning curve is unforgiving. Room count, egress, parking, bathroom ratios, city occupancy rules, the finish standard operators expect — get one wrong and a good deal becomes an expensive education.

This program exists so you don't pay for that education with your own capital. How the program works →

blocks.heading: Who actually lives in these houses

columns.body:
Amazon drivers. Healthcare aides. Restaurant workers. People who just transferred to a new city. Veterans. Older adults on fixed incomes.

A third of Americans can't afford a studio or a one-bedroom apartment, and the deposits and credit requirements keep climbing. These are working people who need a clean, safe place to live that they aren't ashamed of.

That's why the houses are built the way they are. Granite, stainless, tiled showers, smart locks, a ceiling fan in every room. Not a boarding house and not a dorm — a member should walk in feeling like they got the better end of the deal.

You can build a business that returns well and houses people decently. We've never accepted that those are different projects.

blocks.heading: What a finished one looks like
blocks.lede: Not renderings. Houses we've converted, furnished, and put into service.

blocks.heading: Two ways in
blocks.lede: The model has two sides. Operators build the houses. Investors buy them. Both sides are qualified before we put a deal in front of anyone.

items.title: Build one of our houses
items.body: Same as any flip — you buy it, finance it, run your crew, own every decision. We coach the process, certify the finished property, and list it on our marketplace where registered buyers can find it.
items.note: Requires: 10–15 completed flips, your own crew, your own capital.

items.title: Buy a finished property
items.body: Register to see certified co-living properties as they're listed — converted, furnished, and documented to our standards, without running the renovation yourself.
items.note: Requires: proof of funds or financing in place.

blocks.heading: Think you're a fit? Tell us about your work.
blocks.body: We're looking for operators with 10 to 15 flips behind them and a crew already running. Send us your background and we'll tell you straight whether the program makes sense for you right now.
